newsitem.title: FRANCE: SEB says bid for Brazil's Arno fails.
newsitem.headline: SEB says bid for Brazil's Arno fails.

text.p: French domestic appliance maker SEB said on Friday that its public offer for 45 percent of the preference shares of Brazilian appliance manufacturer Arno had failed due to a lack of sufficient shares tendered.
SEB added that it had not yet made a decision on its next step.
"Almost none of the shares were tendered in the public takeover offer. Now we are thinking about what we are going to do," an SEB spokesman said.
The offer launched by the group for 45 percent of Arno's shares expired on Thursday.

SEB had announced on March 20 that it had struck a deal with a group of Arno shareholders holding 31.1 percent of Arno's capital. It had also reached deals enabling it to take control of 97.8 percent of Arno shares with voting rights and 10 percent of shares without voting rights.
But just this last option was exercised, leaving SEB today with 10 percent of Arno's capital.
